transcript:
Header: 
Date: 2026-11-18 16:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Meeting: Hosted API embeddings + rerank demo - Brightnote
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Samir Rao (Brightnote, Head of Search), Emily Park (Brightnote, ML Eng), Janelle Cruz (Brightnote, PM)

Summary (auto): quick hosted api walkthrough focused on embeddings + rerank for Brightnote search relevance. Covered API calls, console demo, rerank endpoint behavior, evaluation plan and POC scope. Customer has existing vector store (Pinecn or Pinho? - transcription uncertain) and is sensitive to latency and data residency.

00:00:05 Alyssa: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm alyssa from redwood inference, i'm the a-e on your account, joining today i've got marco diaz who's our se and he'll run through the console and the rerank examples, excited to learn about your search pain points.
00:00:28 Samir: yep thanks, uh quick context - we're migrating from a mix of elastic + custom dense retrieval, want to improve relevance for long tail queries and reduce manual tuning. Our main constraints are p95 latency under 250ms and costs under existing spend by ~20%.
00:00:52 Marco: cool, that lines up. We'll demo hosted api embeddings endpoint, then the rerank endpoint that runs a lightweight reranker on top of your candidate set. We'll also show console quickstarts and optimize suggestions for batching and caching.
00:01:15 Emily: small note, we use a managed vector DB right now (we think it's pinecone) and we keep embeddings in our VPC. curious about data retention and kms options for hosted.
00:01:33 Alyssa: yes, we have options - hosted with encryption at rest, bring-your-own-kms for dedicated/private options, and audit logs for enterprise. We'll share security deck.

00:02:05 Marco: demo start - here is the hosted api docs (shows curl). embeddings endpoint: POST /v1/embeddings, model: redwood-search-embedding-1536, dim 1536 typical. here's a sample payload and response (embedding vector truncated).
00:02:40 Samir: when you say 1536, is that fixed? our existing model is 1024 dim from older pipeline, will mixing dims be a problem?
00:03:00 Marco: mixing dims isn't supported in a single index; we recommend re-encoding or using cross-embedding mapping. For POC we usually standardize on 1536 for better cosine behavior. also you can use dot product if your vector store prefers.
00:03:30 Janelle: can you talk about rerank - is it a second pass model or inline scoring?
00:03:48 Marco: rerank is a second-pass endpoint. workflow: candidate retrieval from your vector store -> pass top-k (e.g., 50) to /v1/rerank with query + candidates -> rerank returns scored list, supports feature inputs and structured outputs. It's fast because it runs a compact transformer with kv-cache optimizations; expect additional latency typical 30-120ms depending on k.
00:04:20 Emily: what's the cost profile? we care about per-request token cost vs embedding cost across large volumes (hundreds of thousands/day).
00:04:35 Alyssa: embeddings are billed per-embedding unit and rerank as a per-inference unit. For POC we'll model expected qps; Marco can provide batching and caching suggestions to reduce unit cost by up to 3x.
00:05:05 Marco: show console - route config for hosted api, per-model dashboards, latency heatmaps and token-cost breakdown. here we recommend setting threshold for fallback to smaller reranker to keep p95 stable.
00:05:45 Samir: on caching - do you support prefix caching or k-v cache reuse across sessions?
00:06:02 Marco: yes, inference runtime supports kv cache reuse for chat-style flows and prefix caching for repeated queries, for embeddings we recommend vector-level caching. we can also deploy a dedicated cache layer in front of the reranker for identical top-k sets.
00:06:30 Janelle: the app is multi-tenant - we need RBAC and SSO - can hosted do SAML and role scoping?
00:06:45 Alyssa: hosted supports SSO (SAML/OIDC) for the console and api keys, RBAC for project-level roles; for stricter controls we offer Dedicated and Private with VPC peering and customer-managed control plane.
00:07:15 Emily: any compliance artifacts? SOC2? iso?
00:07:22 Alyssa: yes SOC2 type II, ISO 27001 in progress, we'll attach SOC2 report and data processing addendum.

00:08:00 Marco: back to rerank details - example payload: query, candidates array with text+metadata, optional features like BM25 score, domain signal; we support hybrid scoring in the rerank request (combine your vector score + reranker prediction). that helps with blending lexical + semantic.
00:08:38 Samir: that hybrid approach sounds promising since we still rely on lexical signals for dates and sku ids.
00:08:50 Marco: exactly - you can send the original lexical score as a feature. weight tuning can be done via the optimize tool which suggests small grid sweeps and evaluates mrr and recall.

00:09:30 Marco: live example - i call embeddings endpoint with a sample query, then call vector DB (simulated) to get top-50, then call rerank. here's p95 on our test rig ~120ms for rerank with k=50. note the transcription may misstate numbers.
00:10:05 Emily: are there memory requirements for local tokenization and encoding? we plan to run some offline batch indexing.
00:10:20 Marco: batch encoding is fine - embeddings endpoint supports batch size up to 512 but we recommend 128 for stable throughput. you can also use our bulk-embed CLI to stream directly into S3 or your vector DB.
00:10:50 Samir: curious about evaluation - how should we measure success for POC?
00:11:05 Alyssa: typical POC metrics: mrr at k=10, p@5, latency p95, and qualitative feedback from product. We can instrument via the console and run A/B on a subset of traffic.

00:11:40 Marco: now switch to optimize - shows suggestions tab: quantization recommendation for the reranker, batching suggestion for embeddings, and a note to enable caching for repeated queries. also a cost-vs-latency curve.
00:12:05 Janelle: for the POC timeline - we expect a 2-week scoped trial. sample size - maybe 100k queries and 5k priority queries for eval.
00:12:20 Alyssa: that's doable - we usually do a 2-week pilot: week 1 ingestion and baseline, week 2 run experiments and provide results. we'll run a benchmark on your dataset to measure mrr lift and latency.

00:12:58 Samir: security follow-up: we store customer PII in doc text - will hosted ever see raw documents?
00:13:12 Alyssa: hosted processes data; we have contractual terms and can offer Private deployment so data never leaves your VPC for sensitive workloads. for hosted we offer strict retention and opt-out options and can discuss field-level redaction.

00:13:40 Marco: note about vector store integration - we provide client wrappers for pinecone, milvus, we also have export helpers for elastic approximate nearest. if you're using a custom store we'll work with you on adapter.
00:14:05 Emily: about latency - if we need p95 < 200ms for search, is hosted feasible?
00:14:20 Marco: yes in many cases. typical flow: embedding lookup in vector DB (depends on vector DB p95), rerank p95 adds overhead. we recommend colocating vector db in same region and using small k for production, plus enabling optimized kernels. if you need strict p95 with zero external dependency we suggest Dedicated where we can host the vector store and reranker in same cluster.

00:15:00 Samir: can we run a smoke benchmark with our queries?
00:15:10 Alyssa: yes - next steps we'll have Marco send a benchmark checklist and scripts. You provide a sample query set + ground truth; we'll run baseline vs redwood rerank and share metrics.

00:15:45 Marco: quick demo of rerank payload variation: you can pass structured metadata and role-specific prompts; the reranker can return explanations (short text) but note that we don't guarantee faithfulness - it's an aid. also we support function-like structured outputs for downstream UI.
00:16:25 Janelle: did you mention caching top-k sets? that could reduce rerank calls a lot for repetitive queries.
00:16:40 Marco: yes exactly - if top-k vectors don't change often you can cache the ranked result for short TTLs. optimize tool will detect repeated keys and suggest cache TTLs.

00:17:05 Emily: any quotas or rate limits for embeddings? we have bursts during batch indexing.
00:17:20 Alyssa: hosted accounts have rate limits but we can provision burst or move to Dedicated for high sustained throughput. for the POC we can lift limits temporarily.

00:18:00 Samir: what about model drift and monitoring?
00:18:12 Marco: console has quality monitoring - you can upload labeled prompts/evals and we'll alert on regressions vs baseline; there's a rollback flow to revert model version.

00:19:00 Alyssa: let's recap - we'll send pricing + POC scope; Marco share benchmark scripts; Brightnote to provide sample queries and top-k labels. target kickoff next week.

00:19:40 Samir: sounds good. quick nit - can the rerank incorporate click signals as features?
00:19:52 Marco: yes include click-through or dwell time as numeric features in the rerank request. that'll help tune ranking for your business metric.

00:20:20 Janelle: what about vendor lock in for rerank models? if we want to move on-prem later?
00:20:30 Alyssa: we support Private deployment and Dedicated; we also provide exportable model artifacts and model-agnostic features so migration is feasible, we'll include migration notes in the security deck.

00:21:05 Emily: one more on vector dimensionality - if we move to 1536 and reindex, do you have tools to help migration?
00:21:20 Marco: we'll share bulk re-embed tools and an S3-backed job to reencode and push into your vector DB, plus incremental reindex helpers.

00:22:00 Marco: live Q/A - customer asks about error handling on partial failures; rerank supports partial results and fallback to lexical bucket or smaller model. there's also an auto-fallback policy in route config.
00:22:32 Samir: ok good. also curious about logging - we need audit logs showing which model version served which request for compliance.
00:22:45 Alyssa: console's audit logs show token-level and request-level logs; for enterprise customers we can extend retention and deliver logs to your SIEM.

00:23:10 Marco: now demo: rerank edge-case - long docs, we chunk and create passage embeddings and then aggregate. we showed a small script for passage retrieval + rerank to prevent hallucination in long docs.
00:23:48 Emily: any recommended k for passage retrieval?
00:23:55 Marco: usually 5-20 passages depending on doc size. recommended to keep reranker k moderate.

00:24:30 Samir: I want to know expected p95 variance in production - do you have SLO guarantees?
00:24:45 Alyssa: for Hosted we publish typical p95 ranges; SLA-backed guarantees are part of Dedicated contracts. We'll share latency profiles per model in the docs.

00:25:15 Janelle: ok for POC we'll start with hosted and then evaluate Dedicated if latency or residency needs require it.

00:25:40 Marco: technical note - rerank model uses optimized kernels and supports mixed precision quantization; you can trade a bit of accuracy for 2x cost reduction in some workloads. Optimize will propose quant profiles.

00:26:15 Samir: what's the expected engineering effort to integrate?
00:26:25 Alyssa: usually 1-2 engineers for a week for ingestion + basic search pipeline integration, depending on your readiness. for the POC we provide playbooks and a SE-to-SE support window.

00:27:00 Emily: okay send the playbook.

00:27:10 Alyssa: action items - we'll email pricing, security docs, and the POC scope. Marco will run a small benchmark and share results.

00:27:45 Samir: thanks everyone, this was helpful.

00:28:05 Marco: demo end - follow-ups as noted.

Notes on transcription: occasional name mis-hears (Pinecone heard as "Pinecn"), numbers may be approximate. There was some cross-talk between samir and emily around 00:10.

Recap/Next steps: Alyssa to send pricing + POC proposal by 11/20; Marco to send benchmark scripts by 11/19; Brightnote to provide sample queries and labels by 11/22. Plan for 2-week POC kickoff week of 2026-11-23.

References shared: link: /redwood/docs/hosted-embeddings, link: /redwood/benchmarks/poc-checklist, security deck (attached in follow-up email).
